# Marked-block write protocol

Read by Step 5 before writing anything. Every write this skill makes is
either a marked-block merge (three targets) or a whole-file existence gate
(one target) — never a blind overwrite.

## The marker pair this skill owns

```
<!-- BEGIN cep-onboarding-index (auto-generated by ult-onboarding-index, do not edit) -->
...
<!-- END cep-onboarding-index -->
```

Used verbatim, unchanged, in all three merge targets below. Never alter the
marker text itself — a mismatched marker on a re-run would orphan the old
block instead of replacing it.

## Merge targets (marked-block splice)

**`AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`** — each
follows the same decision tree:

1. Read the target file if it exists.
2. If this skill's marker pair is already present, replace only the content
   between those markers, byte-for-byte. Everything outside the markers —
   including, in `AGENTS.md`'s case, `install.sh`'s own installer block
   (see below) — is left untouched.
3. If the marker pair is absent but the file exists, **append** the new
   block at the end of the file, preceded by a blank line. Never interleave
   into or reorder existing content.
4. If the file doesn't exist at all, create it containing just the marked
   block.

`onboarding_index.py merge-block` implements exactly this — see Step 5 for
the invocation.

## `AGENTS.md`'s other owner — never touch it

`install.sh`'s `merge_agents_md()` function (`install.sh` lines ~199-260)
already writes a *different* marked block into the same file, delimited by:

```
<!-- BEGIN context-engineering-protocol SKILLS (auto-generated, do not edit) -->
<!-- END context-engineering-protocol SKILLS -->
```

That block lists which skills are installed in the target repo — it has no
knowledge of CEP *content* artifacts and is a completely separate concern
from this skill's index. Rule: never reason about, parse, or modify
anything inside `context-engineering-protocol SKILLS` markers. Treat that
byte range as off-limits, the same way you'd treat a `.gitignore`d file —
present, real, not yours to touch.

## `.github/copilot-instructions.md`'s other reader

`compiling-project-guidelines/SKILL.md` Step 1 already globs
`.github/copilot-instructions.md` as a guideline *source* and folds its
content into `COMPILED-GUIDELINES.md`. Using this skill's own marker pair
here (rather than raw unmarked prose) keeps the pointer content clearly
attributable as generated-by-this-skill, not a hand-written guideline —
even though `compiling-project-guidelines` doesn't currently special-case
the marker text itself. That's an acceptable, low-cost gap to leave for a
future pass, not a blocker for this skill.

## Whole-file existence gate (one target)

**`.cursor/rules/onboarding.mdc`** is a whole new file, not a shared one —
no marker block needed. `onboarding_index.py write-stub`:

1. If the file already exists, do nothing. Report it as skipped/left alone.
2. If it doesn't exist, write the rendered template as the entire file
   content.

This mirrors `ult-autoscaffold-content`'s stricter posture (never touch a
target that already has real content, full stop) rather than the
marked-block approach — there's no shared-file concern here to justify the
extra complexity of a marker pair.
